carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.name: Mob AI Optimizations
carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.desc: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group mobAiOptimizations and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.name: Ender Pearl Optimizations
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.desc: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group enderPearlOptimizations and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
carpet.rule.tntExplosionOptimizations.de: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group tntExplosionOptimizations and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
carpet.rule.killedTriggerLimitPerTick.na: Killed advancement trigger limit per tick
carpet.rule.killedTriggerLimitPerTick.de: Limits KilledTrigger.trigger executions per tick with one shared budget for all entities.
carpet.rule.killedTriggerLimitPerTick.ex: 0 means unlimited; all dimensions, players and KilledTrigger types share the budget
Calls exceeding the limit are skipped rather than deferred; their advancement checks and completion rewards do not run
carpet.rule.netherPortalCacheDistance.na: Nether portal exit search cache distance
carpet.rule.netherPortalCacheDistance.de: Caches exit portal positions per entrance portal block while entities remain within this distance of the last actual search position and the exit chunk has not changed.
carpet.rule.netherPortalCacheDistance.ex: 0 disables caching; distance is measured as the three-dimensional Euclidean distance in the source world.
carpet.rule.optimizedEquipmentDrops.name: Equipment drop optimization
carpet.rule.optimizedEquipmentDrops.desc: Skips equipment drop enchantment calculations for empty mob equipment slots and context creation for enchantments without equipment drop effects.
carpet.rule.optimizedEquipmentDrops.extr: Empty equipment slots no longer run equipment drop enchantment effects, which may change random number consumption for custom random enchantment effects
Experience orb spawn merge query optimization
Stops the experience orb spawn merge query after the first orb matching vanilla merge conditions.
Preserves vanilla query order, random grouping, experience value matching, and merge logic
carpet.rule.optimizedEntityCollection.de: Uses a section-local spatial index to optimize Lithium push candidate collection. Entity iteration order may change.
carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.betterNoA: Skips AI logic (Mob.serverAiStep) for entities carrying the NoBrainAI NBT tag, while keeping passive motion such as gravity, fluids, entity pushing, crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons and riding. Unlike vanilla NoAI, the entity does not freeze in mid-air.
/data merge entity <target> {NoBrainAI:1b} to set, {NoBrainAI:0b} or /data remove entity <target> NoBrainAI to clear; the tag is saved with the entity and can also be written in /summon NBT
Skipped: target selector, goal selector, navigation, sensing, brain, and movement/look/jump controls

Kept: gravity and ground friction, water and bubble columns, entity pushing and crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons, riding (a player can still steer the mount), burning, item pickup, distance-based despawn

Note: the AI-independent noActionTime no longer accumulates, so the entity will not despawn from 600 ticks of inactivity near a player (same as vanilla NoAI); bosses such as the Ender Dragon or Wither stop their phase progression while tagged
carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.mobAIDela: Chance for a whitelisted mob to have its AI temporarily disabled. The roll happens once, the first time the entity is about to run AI; only when the random value is below this chance is the AI suppressed. Passive motion (gravity, fluids, entity pushing, crush damage, explosion knockback, pistons, riding) is kept.
0 (default) disables the feature entirely; an empty entity list also disables it. Suggested values: 0 and 0.1 (the rule does not restrict the value, anything between 0 and 1 works)
The roll result is stored in the entity's MobAi NBT field, so reloading a chunk never re-rolls it; every entity is decided exactly once

Whitelist of mobs eligible for AI delays, wrapped in braces and comma-separated. Entries are entity ids (minecraft:pig) or entity type tags (#zombies); prefix an entry with ! to exclude it. A list with only exclusions means 'everything except those'; {} disables the feature.

Example: {minecraft:pig,#zombies,!#undead} - pigs and zombie-like mobs, but never undead ones. Suggested values: {!minecraft:drowned} (default, every mob except drowned) and {!minecraft:drowned,!minecraft:piglin}
Matching: union of all positive entries, minus every negative entry; hitting any positive entry is enough
Tags are data-pack tags matched by name; a tag that is not loaded behaves as an empty set (matches nothing)
How many ticks a suppressed entity stays without AI before its AI is restored; must be a positive number.
Counted in ticks experienced by the entity and saved with it (the remaining time is exactly the MobAi NBT field)
A negative remaining time means 'decided: AI is not suppressed' - that is also the state after the AI has been restored
carpet.rule.commandSpawnWhitedListedPlay: Used to summon fake players without prefix
/player <name> spawn original - summon a fake player without prefix
carpet.rule.commandExceedChunkMarker.des: Controls the permission level of ECM command. Invalid when ECM is not started.
carpet.rule.commandExceedChunkMarker.ext: /exceedChunkMarker <dimension> - Show information of the selected dimension
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] setTopY <topY> - Set the ECM height of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] clear - Clear ECM data of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
/exceedChunkMarker [dimension] loadFromWorld - Load ECM data from world data of the selected dimension (dimension defaults to the player's current dimension)
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.desc: Command to view and control entity IDs
carpet.rule.commandLoadedChunkFinder.des: Records connected chunks that are active during a certain period, used to find forgotten chunk loaders.
carpet.rule.commandLoadedChunkFinder.ext: /loadedChunkFinder - Record chunk loading in the current dimension within 1 tick
/loadedChunkFinder <dimension> [tick] - Record chunk loading in the specified dimension for a specified duration, tick defaults to 1
carpet.rule.commandPacketLoggerPlus.desc: Records the pre-compression size of various packets.
carpet.rule.commandPacketLoggerPlus.extr: /packetLogger stop - Stop recording and display data
carpet.rule.commandRequirementModify.des: Modify permission requirements of specified commands
carpet.rule.commandRequirementModify.ext: /requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> set - Set the permission requirement of the specified command to the given permission
/requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> add - Add a permission requirement on top of the existing requirements
/requirementModify <commandPath> <permission> or - Add an OR-condition permission requirement on top of the existing requirements
/requirementModify <commandPath> clear - Clear permission modifications for the specified command
/requirementModify clearAll - Clear permission modifications for all commands
/requirementModify list - List all commands with modified permission requirements
For commandPath, use <> to indicate parameters:
means setting the permission requirement of "player <player> shadow" to ops
carpet.rule.commandRulesSearcher.desc: Adds a subcommand 'search' to carpet, allowing to search carpet rules by keyword
carpet.rule.commandRulesSearcher.extra.0: /carpet search <key> [isNoDefaultValue] [category] - Search carpet rules, key is the search keyword, isNoDefaultValue whether to search only rules with changed default value (default false), category is the rule category
carpet.rule.commandTickSprintFull.desc: Adds a 'full' argument to /tick sprint that prints the duration of every game tick while sprinting
/tick sprint <time> full - Sprint for the given time and print each tick's duration
Prints a duration summary (average/p50/p95/p99/max/tps) when the sprint ends
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.ende: (Deprecated - the better pearl loading ticket can replace it with better results) Applies new loading logic to ender pearls whose speed is above a certain threshold; this is more stable and requires fewer loaded chunks.
The set value indicates the self-loading speed threshold. Set to a negative value to disable.
For pearls with the new loading logic, the loading behavior differs significantly from vanilla.
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.exce: Prerequisite for raycast optimization, may cause additional storage (generally only increases save size by less than 0.1%)
When enabling for the first time, be sure to load once with /exceedChunkMarker
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.opti: Optimizes raycast via ECM. Ensure ECM is enabled and has been loaded from the save before turning on.
Known feature: Projectiles will ignore entity hitboxes at some specific positions.
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.bett: Replaces the vanilla loading ticket with a special loading ticket in certain cases. When ECM is not enabled, it only applies to pearls outside world height.
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.opti: In most cases, stops flying high-speed pearls from generating new chunks, which can greatly reduce save size. When ECM is not enabled, only pearls outside world height will not generate chunks.
Known feature: Pearls will ignore entity hitboxes that are not loaded.
carpet.rule.tntExplosionOptimizations.op: Once this many explosions hit the same point within one game tick, the block calculation is skipped when a worst-case check proves no block can be destroyed; only entities are affected
Only same-tick explosions with identical coordinates and power
carpet.rule.tntExplosionOptimizations.me: A more aggressive TNT merging scheme, may cause unexpected results. Cannot be used together with other TNT merging rules.
carpet.rule.tntExplosionOptimizations.tn: Optimizes TNT entities by removing unnecessary TNT entity packets (Fuse) and reducing packet frequency
carpet.rule.packetLimits.name: Packet limits
carpet.rule.packetLimits.desc: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group packetLimits and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
carpet.rule.packetLimits.entitySpawnLimi: Reduces the tracking range of subsequent entities when too many entities of the same type are added in one world during the same tick.
Requires packetLimits; a negative value disables the per-tick limit
carpet.rule.packetLimits.limitedEntityTr: Tracking range in blocks for entities exceeding the per-tick threshold.
carpet.rule.packetLimits.entitySpawnLimi: Probabilistically prevents tracking based on the number of same-type entities added in the same chunk during the previous one-second window.
Requires packetLimits; a negative value disables this limit; one second is 20 game ticks
carpet.rule.packetLimits.entityTrackingR: Restores the original tracking range of entities limited by either threshold once their age reaches this many game ticks.
A negative value disables automatic recovery; disabling the master switch still restores limited entities
carpet.rule.packetLimits.particlePacketR: Sending range in blocks for non-forced particle packets.
Requires packetLimits; disabling it restores the vanilla range of 32 blocks
Forced particle packets keep their vanilla range of 512 blocks
carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.piglinLoo: Only items that have been present for a certain time will be picked up by piglins
carpet.rule.mobAiOptimizations.piglinSta: For piglins stacked to a certain amount, suppress AI of some of them.
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.0: /entityID - Show the next 5 entity IDs to be generated
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.1: /entityID show <count> - Show the specified number of entity IDs to be generated
carpet.rule.commandEntityID.extra.2: /entityID show <beginID> <endID> - Show entity IDs within the specified range
carpet.rule.commandEntityIDSet.extra.0: /entityID set <id> - Set the current entity ID to the specified value
carpet.rule.optimizedFakePlayerTick.desc: Trims client sync/advancement/stats/Waypoint per-tick logic for Carpet fake players, keeping main-hand item tick and behavior simulation
carpet.rule.optimizedFakePlayerTick.extr: May affect fake player stats, advancements, scoreboard auto-sync and locator bar display
carpet.rule.naturalSpawningOptimizations: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group naturalSpawningOptimizations and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
Whitelist of dimensions whose spawn statistic is simplified, wrapped in braces and comma-separated; {} simplifies nothing
Simplification skips the chunk lookup and the biome query inside the spawn statistic
The result stays identical to vanilla only when no biome of the world defines spawn costs
Reuses the natural-spawning candidate chunk list, refreshed every 40 gt; when disabled, vanilla iteration is used
Precomputes natural-spawning candidates off-thread; entity creation and counting stay on the main thread
Falls back to vanilla when data is unavailable or stale
carpet.rule.randomTickOptimizations.name: Random Tick Optimizations
carpet.rule.randomTickOptimizations.desc: Master switch; configure members with /carpet group randomTickOptimizations and save them in carpet-rof-addition.json
carpet.rule.randomTickOptimizations.rand: Reuses the random-tick chunk list, refreshed every 40 gt; when disabled, vanilla iteration is used
carpet.rule.randomTickOptimizations.asyn: Precomputes the next tick's random-tick candidates off-thread; falls back to vanilla when the result is invalid
carpet.rule.enderPearlOptimizations.bloc: Makes a pearl's chunk loading block the main thread, reducing desync between pearl ticks and world ticks.
The maximum blocking time in milliseconds; set to 0 to disable.
carpet.rule.tntExplosionOptimizations.me: TRUE: old explosion handling; moving merged TNT behaves unlike vanilla
SAFE: safer explosion handling; moving merged TNT behaves like vanilla
AlmostVanilla: merges only when TNT explodes, keeping TNT tick order
AlmostVanilla should not change TNT behaviour; report any vanilla mismatch as an issue
SafePlus: merges only at explosion time like AlmostVanilla, but the decision is made in a once-per-tick pre-pass over adjacent same-position TNTs, without rewriting entity tick order
Merges the multiple explosions produced by one merged TNT into a single explosion, so entities are affected only once. Only applies when TNT merging and explosion optimization are both enabled.
Requires mergeTNTNext to be a mode other than False
Damage is applied once; knockback is scaled by the merge count, so the total push matches vanilla
